reviews.title: Best value for money
reviews.comment: Amazing case both aesthetic wise and practicality, has much room for bulky GPUS, airflow is great too, comes with complete cable management accessories. A little tricky for PSU fitment and  cables, larger PSU will be hard to fit and can press against IO cables.

reviews.title: Excellent GAMING CASE W RGB FANS
reviews.comment: I have been building computers for over 40 years now and I have had a lot of different cases with a gaming theme.  This one is one of my favorites and it is very easy to build in and make changes afterwards which always seems to be the case after I complete a build. It looks great and the fans are top notch and the airflow is good also keeping my 13600K at a very low temperature. 32c in case anyone wants to know and this is using a COOLMASTER 212 APEX CPU AIR COOLER.
reviews.author: “ SCOTT”

reviews.title: Stylish and Practical, Requires Planning
reviews.comment: Excellent case if you're looking for a more straight edge design that is flashy without being gaudy over over-presenting. It has a nice mix of aesthetics, enough room in the back to build in, but you have to make sure you pre-plan because it's a nightmare if you don't. One of the smallest ATX cases that fits a 420 AIO and an EATX motherboard, though I would definitely recommend a regular ATX motherboard. And you CAN build this with a lian li-edge PSU you just have to unscrew the left most usb-a (which I would have done anyways to give data to the edge's included fan hub.) It was easy to take apart, easy to build in, and easy to cable manage after building in. Everything is toolless and the most you will need tools for is to "break" the factory tightened hand-screws, after that you can practically build and rebuild it with no problems whatsoever. Their customer service is quick to respond and very kind as well, answering all of my questions within 24 hours. I would purchase this case as well as other cases they make in the future.
reviews.author: ronda h.

reviews.title: Highly Recommended - Use a Small Power Supply
reviews.comment: There are plenty of reviews you can find online for this case (Kitguru, Robeytech, PCMag etc.) and you ought to look at them before you buy. I’ll agree with some and disagree with others. First, this case is NOT difficult to build in if you buy a SMALL power supply – I bought a SFF. People complain about not having enough wiring space – I had no trouble – maybe it’s because I planned everything before I started (thanks MaximumPC). I’ve never had such a clean looking build before (look at the pictures) and I’ve been building PC’s for a long time. Yes, you will have to take out one of the lower fans to access the fan/RGB headers depending on your motherboard (and if you buy the case with the fans included…obviously) but that’s pretty standard. Yes, you may need to run your wiring a different way than you have before (assuming you have done previous builds) but if your power supply comes with short cables you don’t have to buy extensions or specialized cables from MODDIY. I ran the GPU wiring over the GPU rather than under because the Gen 5 12VHPWR PSU cable that came with the power supply was really short (sorry Corsair) – but the power supply is right there, so it’s not an issue.  Yes, the shipping packaging is not great – the first one I ordered came with the plastic bottom broken, and the second with the RGB on the back fan not functioning. Amazon replaced the first and Geometric Future replace the fan (I received 3 fans a couple of days after I posted the problem to the seller’s comments – I’d say that’s pretty superior customer support). I may have just been unlucky, but I thought you should know of my experience. Yes, there are some minor misalignments (e.g. the thumb screw on the power supply bracket does not line up very well... as noted by Kitguru) but overall, the build quality is very good, the case is sturdy, and the finish is stylish. I've had no issues with cooling and consistent with online reviews, air flow is excellent. The bottom line, you might have to use your brain a little bit, but once you’re finished, you will have a great looking machine inside and out. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Dave P.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.comment: I love this case! This is the kind of layout I have been looking for over a decade. Pros: Layout. The case fits a ton of cooling in a standard mid tower size. 420mm rad support on top. Value Will fit even the insane-sized gpus. Build quality is good for the price features. I'd say about NZXT level (2021 h5 flow) build quality. Better than Thermaltake (tower 200). Worse than Phanteks (enthoo pro and enthoo evolv) and lian li (v3000+). Basically, sturdy and well-built, but not luxurious. Easy to build inside of (assuming you don't have tons of HDD/SSD to mount/wire - there are better options for data/server/nas cases). Chimney style cooling. Great airflow. Light weight for how sturdy it is. Fits in a server rack when laid on its side Cons: The PSU cage limits your options, especially if looking at a power-hungry equipment like the 5090. I had been looking at this case for a while but wanted 1200W for future gpu. The Montech century II 1200W recently released and reviewed very well at hardware busters, is very good value, and fits the size limitations. If you want to switch off the power button on the PSU, you have to remove the top panel (but removal would be easy in most circumstances). Depending on your situation, you may want to purchase a filter kit. The bottom intake is the only part that is filtered, and it is a pretty open case. Due to the high air flow, it can get loud depending on your fans and fan curves. Hard to find 160mm fans for the front fan (optional) Honestly, the unknowns of this brand and seemingly buried coverage might scare you off. But this is a great case. Some of the YouTube reviews are perplexing. I think these product schills just did not get paid for their review and decided to bash things that were not even relevant or correct.
